- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +1.00 or +0.50) and news volume spikes, model tends to overreact — overshoots true price by 1–3% in next 3–5 days; correct by reducing forecast by 0.5–1.5 standard deviations.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment (e.g., +1.00 followed by +0.50), model often fails to mean-revert — forecasts remain elevated for 2–4 days; apply downward bias of 0.3–0.7x the spike magnitude.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.33 to -1.00) and news volume drops, model underreacts — forecasts lag behind true price by 1–2 days; adjust by adding 0.2–0.5x the magnitude of the negative sentiment shift.
- When sentiment change is negative and news volume is low (e.g., -0.33 with 0.0 news), model underestimates downside risk — forecast is 1–2% too low; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for hidden volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates price during high sentiment periods — apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction if sentiment > 0.67 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment change is +0.33 or higher and news volume is high, model tends to overfit recent trends — apply 0.3–0.7% downward adjustment to prevent over-optimism.
